title: Maple Leafs sign Sergei Bobrovsky to 3-year, $7 million AAV contract: Sources
author: Jesse Granger
content:
The Toronto Maple Leafs signed goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract, according to league sources who spoke on the condition of anonymity to address negotiations that aren’t public.

Bobrovsky will be 38 before the 2026-27 season begins, and is coming off a down year playing behind a Florida Panthers team decimated by injuries. He posted career-worst numbers in save percentage (.877) and goals saved above expected (-17.6).

While it was a down year for the likely future Hockey Hall of Famer, Bobrovsky is only a year removed from anchoring the Panthers to three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, with two wins, and he is one of the most decorated goalies of this generation. Bobrovsky won two Vezina Trophies, with Columbus in 2013 and 2017, and leads all active goalies with 456 career wins.

The Russian netminder’s recent postseason resume is equally impressive. His 44 wins since 2023 aren’t just the most in the NHL; they’re 12 clear of the next-closest goalie. He has a .912 playoff save percentage and a league-best 26.14 goals saved above expected over that span. His 61 career playoff wins rank second among active goalies, and 16th all-time.

It’s not hard to see what the Leafs are thinking here.

They are desperate to turn things around in a major way next season and hopefully keep captain Auston Matthews around because of it.

In Bobrovsky, they net a goalie with a rich resume in the NHL, including two Stanley Cup titles as the Florida Panthers No. 1. He’s going to play and play a lot, and if the Leafs can get back in the playoffs, he has a track record of doing the job there.

It’s still a risky bet.

Bobrovsky just had the worst season of his NHL career and he’ll be 38 in September. He’ll be one of the oldest goalies in the league next season and the Leafs will be counting on him to play 50-plus games, plus more in the playoffs potentially.

It’s a big assumption that he simply bounces back to form next season and gives them any kind of value on that contract. — Jonas Siegel
